parts.text: A student is studying the cooling of water. She is using the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record the room temperature θ R as indicated by the thermometer in Fig. 2.1. θ R = ...........................................................[1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student pours approximately 100 cm 3 of hot water into the beaker. She reads the thermometer at the start of the experiment and again at times t = 30 s, 60 s, 90 s, 120 s, 150 s, 180 s, 210 s, 240 s and 270 s. Her readings of the temperature θ are shown in Table 2.1. Complete the table. Table 2.1 t / s θ / °C 0 85.0 82.0 80.0 77.5 75.5 74.0 72.0 70.5 69.0 67.5 [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Calculate the average cooling rate x 1 for the first 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from the table and the equation x 1 = ( θ 0 – θ 90 ) T , where T = 90 s and θ 0 and θ 90 are the temperatures at 0 s and 90 s. Give the unit for the cooling rate. x 1 = ...........................................................[2]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 2 in the next 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from the table and the equation x 2 = ( θ 90 – θ 180 ) T , where T = 90 s and θ 90 and θ 180 are the temperatures at 90 s and 180 s. x 2 = ...............................................................

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 3 in the last 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from the table and the equation x 3 = ( θ 180 – θ 270 ) T , where T = 90 s and θ 180 and θ 270 are the temperatures at 180 s and 270 s. x 3 = ...............................................................
